std.state_tier leaf-first violation (std/holon_std/state_tier/tier.py _add/_release): kids[parent] counts a child only if the parent's copy existed when the child was stored. Under host.admit=evict (and hit:<n>) the device evicts leaves first, so children are stored before parents and the parent counts 0 children; the host level then evicts the interior copy (the core drops the subtree: hits lost). A child dropped later takes the parent's count to -1 (truthy: never a leaf again). Repro on the bare tier of plugins/tests/test_state_tier.py: store (2, parent 1) then (1) with evicting=True, hit([1, 2]), store three more blocks in room for four -> dropped() == [(1, None)] with 2's copy kept.

load-before-store and load-reuse-unwaited cannot change an outcome end to end as planted: D4's free rule (the next launch waits for copies on freed units) and a load's after = the last launched step (whose launch waited on them) order the reading copy after the store; the tier's own write fence only matters when eviction and the reload fall in one schedule. A late H2D into an evicted loading block's units lands before the next writer because a launch waiting on any later load drains the copy stream in order. They never fired (GPU, 0.05 s and 0.3 s delays) or fired without a change (CPU).
swap-onto-lower (promote() called, load skipped) changes nothing on the tiny fp32 models (recomputed and cached bytes give the same greedy outputs) and is caught on Qwen3-8B (17 requests differ).

adopt-source-reused (loaded ignoring the reading step's end) cannot change anything on the CPU (a step's adopt has run by the end of its launch); its join variant fires 269 times on the tiny hybrid without a change (no payload copy is evicted and re-stored between the two adopts).
